name: Legal AI
description: Legal drafting and review assistants compared on the same public documents: an NDA with a buried non-compete, a Swedish employment clause, a DPA gap analysis, a fake citation. The products with no public API get a standing challenge; open models run the bank as proxies in the meantime.

metrics.label: Rubric accuracy
metrics.description: Every prompt ships with a machine-checkable rubric: facts, clause numbers, party names and figures the answer must contain (must_include: substring on lowercased, whitespace-collapsed text, alternatives allowed), values that must appear in a specific shape and structural markers such as a bullet, a heading or a {+tracked change+} (regex, flags im), and citations that must stay inside the source (cites_only). accuracy = 1 + 9 x weighted passes / weighted items over those kinds, rounded to one decimal. No judge model, no estimate: a pass is a substring or a regex match.

metrics.label: Constraint adherence
metrics.description: The prompt's constraints, checked deterministically: must_not_include (a fabricated case endorsed as real, a legalese word the brief banned, a clause number that does not exist), max_words and min_words on a Unicode word count that ignores markdown punctuation, language by a stopword vote (en/sv/de/fr/es), format_json (parses, and carries the required top-level keys) and format_markdown_table. adherence = 1 + 9 x weighted passes / weighted items over those kinds; null when a prompt has none.

metrics.label: Conciseness
metrics.description: Length against the brief, from a formula rather than a judge. target = the smallest max_words item in the prompt's rubric (400 when there is none). 10 when the output is at or under the target; linear down to 1 at three times the target; an empty output is 1. Facts are scored by accuracy, so this metric only measures whether the answer stayed the length the buyer asked for.

metrics.label: Speed
metrics.description: Time to first token and total generation time, ranked against every other run on the same prompt. 10 = fastest, 1 = slowest, linear in between on the mean of the two ranks. Needs at least two tools on a prompt; otherwise blank. Open models run on the same CPU; API proxies are measured from the same host.

rubric_contract.implemented_by: scripts/score-text.py (deterministic, keyless); unit tests in scripts/tests/test_text_rubric.py
rubric_contract.summary: prompts[].rubric is a list of items {id, kind, value, weight?} plus per-kind options. The scorer checks every item against the run's <prompt-id>.md, writes scores.accuracy, scores.adherence, scores.conciseness (1-10, one decimal) and rubric_results into runs.json, and leaves scores.velocity null for the exporter to rank from ttft_ms and latency_ms.
rubric_contract.normalisation: must_include and must_not_include compare on lowercased, whitespace-collapsed text with curly quotes and dashes straightened. regex runs on the raw output with flags 'im' unless the item sets flags. Word count = Unicode word runs (7.2, don't and re-run are one word each; table pipes and markdown punctuation do not count).

kinds.must_include: value: string or list of strings; passes when at least one alternative is present ("match": "all" requires every entry).
kinds.must_not_include: value: string or list; passes when none is present.
kinds.regex: value: pattern or list of patterns; passes when re.search matches any. Optional "flags" (default "im"). Also used for structure: a bullet line, a numbered line, a heading, a [-deleted-] or {+inserted+} span.
kinds.max_words: value: int; passes when words <= value. The smallest max_words is the conciseness target.
kinds.min_words: value: int; passes when words >= value.
kinds.language: value: en | sv | de | fr | es (region tags reduced to the base); passes when the stopword vote picks that language outright, a tie fails.
kinds.format_json: value: true, or a list of required top-level keys; the whole output, a ```json fence or the first {...}/[...] span must parse.
kinds.format_markdown_table: value: true, an int (minimum data rows) or a list of header names; needs a header row, a |---| separator and data rows.
kinds.cites_only: value: list of allowed references (Clause 4, Article 28(3), § 6); every citation the output makes must be one of them; "min" requires a citation count.

rubric_contract.weight: Optional number, default 1. Per group: score = 1 + 9 x sum(weight x pass) / sum(weight), rounded to one decimal (halves up). A group with no items is null. An unknown kind is recorded as failed under adherence, so a typo lowers the score instead of vanishing.
rubric_contract.conciseness: target = min(max_words values) else 400. ratio = words / target. 10 when ratio <= 1; 10 - 9 x (ratio - 1) / 2 between 1 and 3; 1 at ratio >= 3 or for an empty output.
rubric_contract.output_fields: The runner writes output (<prompt-id>.md), output_chars, output_words, tokens_in, tokens_out, ttft_ms, latency_ms, tokens_per_s, model, run_at, status, error. The scorer adds scores.{accuracy,adherence,conciseness}, rubric_results: [{id, kind, group, weight, pass, detail}], output_words, target_words, scored_at. The exporter publishes each rubric_results entry as rubric_hits: [{id, hit, note}] and the output file as output_url plus a 600-character output_excerpt.
rubric_contract.note_field: An item's optional "note" is documentation for readers of the catalog; the scorer ignores it.
